blocks.text: Kimberly Branch has joined the engineering group as a Design Technician. She will draft the grading and drainage sheets, and she will run the quantity takeoffs the engineers need when they price a proposal.

Kimberly reports to Linda George, Project Engineer, who will assign her work and set her schedule. Her takeoffs will feed the proposals directly, so accuracy on a quantity matters as much as speed. A takeoff that is off by a little can turn a fair proposal into a poor one, and the firm would rather she take the extra hour than hand up a number she is unsure of. She is methodical and labels her files plainly, which is a habit this office values; a sheet she has set aside can be found later without anyone having to ask her where it went.

The first weeks are mostly setup. Her station is on the CAD network, the standard-detail library and the takeoff sheets are under the lettered project folders, and time is kept by project number on the weekly sheet. No set leaves the office until Mark Todd has reviewed the drawings and the cover sheet is sealed, and a takeoff that supports a proposal is checked with the same care. She should set up her drawing files and takeoff sheets the firm's way from the start, since a proposal is often revisited months later when the job comes in and the numbers have to be found again. When a quantity does not tie out, she is to raise it with the engineer of record rather than round it away.
To begin, Linda George has a grading takeoff queued for a proposal in progress, and Kimberly can start there while she learns the firm's file conventions.
